nature_of_institutionalization: Institutionalisation is emerging: panels are commissioned by Parliament, with proposals for one per year from 2027 onward.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**CPPP Committee, Embedding Public Participation in the Work of the Parliament, 2nd Report 2023 (Session 6), Recommendation 7 of the Citizens' Panel on Participation (2022)**

7\. Legislate for Deliberative Democracy in order to ensure that: diverse voices and communities from all parts of Scotland influence Scottish Parliament's work, and the public are consistently informed and consulted on local and national issues.

In drawing up this legislation the Parliament should:

- Recognise that there is not one engagement solution that fits all situations and issues.
- Design and implement a framework based on this panel's recommendations for ensuring diverse participation in deliberative democracy.

The framework should include:

- An annually recurring citizens' panel with agenda-setting powers to determine which local and national issues require either national or local people's panels (e.g. deliberative town halls).
- Protection for participants to improve participation. We do not agree that participation in panels should be mandatory, but protective elements such as the right to time off work should be included for people who are selected to take part.
- Rules around how MSPs consider and respond to recommendations from people's panels such as mandatory follow-up to people's panels' recommendations no later than 9 months and a response from the Parliament and Government.
- Potential for mixed MSP–people panels.
- Ability to form local panels with local MSPs with outcomes that are sent up to the national level.

**Bundestag Drucksache 20/6709 (9 May 2023), Section II.1**

The Citizens' Assembly is to comprise 160 persons selected at random from the entire population over the age of 16 years whose main residence is in Germany.

The random selection will be based on a staged, stratified procedure. In that way, a balanced distribution by socio-demographic background, age group, gender, regional origin, municipality size and educational attainment level is to be achieved. In addition, the percentages of the population who are vegetarians and vegans should be reflected in the Citizens' Assembly.

Dem Bürgerrat gehören 160 Personen an, die nach dem Zufallsprinzip aus allen Menschen über 16 Jahren mit Erstwohnsitz in Deutschland ausgewählt werden.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Bundestag Drucksache 20/6709 (9 May 2023)**

The Bundestag is requested to adopt the following motion:

The German Bundestag will appoint a Citizens' Assembly on nutrition in transition: between a private matter and governmental responsibilities.

*Note: this motion is not based on any underlying statute. There is thus not a specific legal basis for the Bundestag to set up citizens' assemblies, and one does not appear to be needed. This point is made since the Bundestag presents citizens' assemblies as a regular tool, which they may be, but not one that requires an underlying statute to establish.*

**Bundestag-Drucksache 20/6709 (9. Mai 2023)**

Der Bundestag wolle beschließen:

Der Deutsche Bundestag setzt einen Bürgerrat „Ernährung im Wandel: Zwischen Privatangelegenheit und staatlichen Aufgaben“ ein.

*Hinweis: Dieser Antrag stützt sich auf kein zugrunde liegendes Gesetz. Es besteht somit keine spezifische gesetzliche Grundlage dafür, dass der Bundestag Bürgerräte einsetzt, und eine solche scheint auch nicht erforderlich zu sein; der Bundestag stellt Bürgerräte als reguläres Instrument dar, das jedoch keiner gesetzlichen Grundlage bedarf.*

nature_of_institutionalization: A Commission recommendation (2023) calling on Member States to promote the participation of citizens and civil society organisations in public policy-making.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2836 (12 December 2023), point 11**

Member States should introduce citizen-led participatory and deliberative exercises on specific decisions and policies, and support and promote individual and collective ways of participation, such as citizens panels, citizens assemblies, and other dialogue and co-creation formats. When doing so, Member States could draw inspiration from the experience, expertise and good practice gathered in the context of the Conference on the Future of Europe, and the subsequent European Citizens' Panels, as well as international standards such as the OECD Guidelines for Public Participation. Member States should ensure that such exercises are facilitated by a robust methodology and core principles supporting their quality, inclusiveness and integrity.

**Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2836 (12 December 2023), point 12**

When inviting citizens to participatory and deliberative citizen engagement exercises, Member States should ensure inclusiveness to the best possible extent. In order to do so, they should use the best available statistical random sampling and sortition techniques. Where possible and as necessary Member States should identify and address differences in participation of different groups by making use of statistics and attitudinal studies. The selection of citizens should be based on demographic criteria, to ensure that the participants reflect the demographic configuration of the Member State including by relying on census or other similar relevant data and any other attitudinal criteria that ensure diversity. Member States should ensure conducive conditions for participation without burden and, where appropriate, the reimbursement of participation costs, including to support economically excluded citizens.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2836 (12 December 2023), point 1**

This Recommendation aims to promote the participation of citizens and civil society organisations in public policy-making to help building democratic resilience within the Union. It encourages Member States to provide more opportunities for citizens and civil society organisations to effectively participate in public policy-making processes carried out by public authorities at the local, regional and national levels, in line with established standards and good practices.

*Note: this is a Commission Recommendation and, under Article 288 TFEU, has no binding force; it encourages rather than requires Member States to act.*

**Citizens' Council of Lisbon (official process description, lisboaparticipa.pt)**

Phases of the process:

1. Choice of theme — the theme is chosen on the basis of the Grand Options Plan of the City of Lisbon.
2. Registration — participation by Lisbon residents in the sessions is subject to registration.
3. Lottery — a lottery conducted independently, through a stratified sampling model and random selection of participants, representative of the population of the City of Lisbon.
4. Sessions — a space for dynamic and informed debate on the defined theme, with the aim that citizens present proposals to the Lisbon City Council.
5. Meeting with the Ambassadors.

*Note: 50 participants per session. The Council has held annual editions since 2022 (2022, 2023, 2024), with a fourth edition on 24 and 31 May 2025.*

**Conselho de Cidadãos de Lisboa (descrição oficial do processo, lisboaparticipa.pt)**

Fases do processo:

1. Escolha do Tema — Tema escolhido com base nas Grandes Opções do Plano da Cidade de Lisboa.
2. Inscrições — A participação dos munícipes de Lisboa nas sessões está sujeita a inscrição.
3. Sorteio — Sorteio realizado de forma independente, através do modelo de amostragem estratificada e seleção aleatória dos participantes, representativa da população da Cidade de Lisboa.
4. Sessões — Espaço de debate dinâmico e informado sobre o tema definido, com o objetivo de os cidadãos apresentarem propostas à Câmara Municipal de Lisboa.
5. Reunião com os Embaixadores.

*Nota: 50 participantes por sessão. O Conselho realizou edições anuais desde 2022 (2022, 2023, 2024) e uma 4.ª edição nos dias 24 e 31 de maio de 2025.*

Um dos pilares das Grandes Opções do Plano 2022-2026 da cidade de Lisboa (Deliberação n.º 16/AML/2022, publicada no 3.º suplemento ao B.M. n.º 1460, de 10/02/2022) assenta, precisamente, numa «cidade participada» através da criação de mecanismos que contribuam para acelerar a participação dos cidadãos.

nature_of_institutionalization: Institutionalised by state law (2021), giving authorities a standing legal framework to conduct dialogical participation with randomly selected citizens in structured formats.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Dialogical Citizen Participation Act (Baden-Württemberg, 2021), § 2**

1. Authorities within the meaning of § 1 of the State Administrative Procedure Act may, within their competence, conduct a dialogical citizen participation on specific topics or projects.
2. The decision on whether to conduct a dialogical citizen participation lies at the discretion of the authorities. This Act confers no entitlement to the conduct of a dialogical citizen participation.
3. Statutory procedural provisions remain unaffected by this Act.
4. The authority must publish its intention to conduct a dialogical citizen participation at least three weeks before participants are invited. This may be done by publication on the authority's website. In doing so it must set out the specific topic or project concerned, the intention of the dialogue and the dialogue format.
5. The dialogical citizen participation may be conducted with participants randomly selected from the population register according to defined criteria. The selection is made from a subset of the population. Only the data listed in § 34(1) of the Federal Registration Act (BMG) may be used as selection criteria; this does not constitute discrimination contrary to the principle of equality. The subset should be large enough that it is expected to contain at least 1,000 persons. Where this number is unlikely to be reached within the authority's local area of competence, the subset may be extended to a larger area and, if necessary, the whole Land, insofar as this is strictly required to achieve the purpose of the specific dialogical citizen participation and authorities in whose local area persons would be included do not object.
6. The randomly selected persons must be asked in writing — with the information required by Article 14(1) and (2) of the GDPR — whether they wish to take part in the dialogical citizen participation. Prospective participants must be given a deadline to reply. Those contacted are free not to follow the invitation, without replying or giving reasons; the letter must point this out. The authority may form a further subset from the acceptances in order to keep the number of participants practicable. In selecting among the acceptances, the authority must have regard to the criteria defined for the random selection and select again by lot. There is no entitlement to participate.

**Gesetz über die dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung (Dialogische-Bürgerbeteiligungs-Gesetz, DBG) (Baden-Württemberg, 2021), § 2**

1. Behörden im Sinne von § 1 LVwVfG können im Rahmen ihrer Zuständigkeit für konkrete Themen oder Vorhaben eine dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung durchführen.
2. Die Entscheidung über die Durchführung einer dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung liegt im Ermessen der Behörden. Es besteht nach diesem Gesetz kein Anspruch auf Durchführung einer dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung.
3. Gesetzliche Verfahrensvorschriften bleiben durch dieses Gesetz unberührt.
4. Die Behörde hat die Absicht, eine dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung durchzuführen, mindestens drei Wochen vor der Einladung von Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern zu veröffentlichen. Dies kann durch Veröffentlichung auf der Internetseite der Behörde geschehen. Sie hat dabei das konkrete Thema oder Vorhaben, zu dem es eine dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung geben soll, sowie die Dialogabsicht und das Dialogformat darzulegen.
5. Die dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung kann mit zufällig nach bestimmten Kriterien aus dem Melderegister ausgewählten Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern durchgeführt werden. Die Auswahl erfolgt aus einer Teilmenge der Bevölkerung heraus. Als Auswahlkriterien können nur die in § 34 Absatz 1 des Bundesmeldegesetzes (BMG) genannten Daten genutzt werden, dies stellt keine gleichheitswidrige Diskriminierung dar. Die Teilmenge soll so groß sein, dass voraussichtlich mindestens 1.000 Personen enthalten sind. Soweit diese Größe einer Personenzahl im örtlichen Zuständigkeitsbereich der Behörde voraussichtlich nicht erreicht werden kann, kann die Teilmenge auf einen örtlich größeren Bereich und bei Bedarf das ganze Land ausgedehnt werden, soweit dies die Erreichung des mit der konkreten dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung verfolgten Zwecks zwingend erfordert und Behörden, in deren örtlichem Zuständigkeitsbereich Personen in die Teilmenge einbezogen werden sollen, nicht widersprechen.
6. Die zufällig ausgewählten Personen sind unter Mitteilung der Informationen gemäß Artikel 14 Absatz 1 und 2 der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DS-GVO) schriftlich zu fragen, ob sie an der dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung teilnehmen möchten. Den möglichen Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern ist eine Frist zur Antwort zu setzen. Es steht den Angeschriebenen frei, ohne Antwort oder ohne Angabe von Gründen, der Einladung nicht zu folgen. Hierauf ist in dem Anschreiben hinzuweisen. Die Behörde kann aus den Zusagen der ausgewählten Personen eine erneute Teilmenge bilden, um die Teilnehmerzahl praktikabel zu halten. Bei der Auswahl der Zusagen hat die Behörde auf die für die Zufallsauswahl definierten Kriterien zu achten und erneut durch Los auszuwählen. Es besteht kein Anspruch auf eine Teilnahme.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Dialogical Citizen Participation Act (Baden-Württemberg, 2021), § 1**

1. The purpose of dialogical citizen participation is to explore needs existing within the population regarding a specific topic or project. This takes place through dialogues between the authority and the public. The outcome of the dialogical citizen participation is recorded in a report. This report is not binding on the responsible bodies.
2. Dialogical citizen participation is an informal part of administrative action and may be conducted outside, before, or alongside an administrative procedure.
3. Dialogical citizen participation may take place in various formats, particularly suitable are discussion forums, round tables, or conferences.
4. Dialogical citizen participation is a public task which may be carried out voluntarily.

**Gesetz über die dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung (Dialogische-Bürgerbeteiligungs-Gesetz, DBG) (Baden-Württemberg, 2021), § 1**

1. Zweck der dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung ist es, Bedürfnisse, die innerhalb der Bevölkerung für ein konkretes Thema oder Vorhaben bestehen, zu erkunden. Dies geschieht durch Dialoge der Behörde mit der Öffentlichkeit. Das Ergebnis der dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung wird in einem Bericht festgehalten. Dieser ist für die zuständigen Stellen nicht bindend.
2. Die dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung ist ein informeller Teil des Verwaltungshandelns und kann außerhalb, vor oder neben einem Verwaltungsverfahren durchgeführt werden.
3. Die Durchführung einer dialogischen Bürgerbeteiligung ist in verschiedenen Formaten möglich, insbesondere geeignet sind Diskussionsforen, Runde Tische oder Konferenzen.
4. Die dialogische Bürgerbeteiligung ist eine öffentliche Aufgabe, die freiwillig wahrgenommen werden kann.

nature_of_institutionalization: 2020 Ordinance No. 7500 creates a citizens' jury to resolve major grievance petitions within 30 days.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Seoul Metropolitan Government Ordinance on the Operation of the Civil Complaints Jury System (Ordinance No. 7500, 2020), art. 6**

- (1) The Mayor may form a candidate jury pool (baesimwon-hubodan) of up to 100 persons, composed of the following:
    - 1\. members of the Committee;
    - 2\. the citizen-participation ombudsmen under art. 25(1) of the Seoul Metropolitan Government Ordinance on the Operation of the Citizen Audit Ombudsman Committee and on Resident Audit Requests;
    - 3\. expert jurors: experts holding the qualifications and practical experience of professors, lawyers, tax accountants, professional engineers (including licensed architects), and the like in fields such as welfare, environment and transport, housing and construction, urban planning, and public conflict;
    - 4\. citizen jurors: persons entitled to vote for members of the Seoul Metropolitan Council and for the Mayor under art. 15(2) of the Public Official Election Act.
- (2) Expert jurors and citizen jurors are appointed by the Mayor, following recommendation by autonomous-district (gu) heads or relevant organisations or open recruitment, and deliberation by the Committee.
- (3) The term of office of expert jurors and citizen jurors is two years, renewable up to twice.

**Seoul Metropolitan Government Ordinance on the Operation of the Civil Complaints Jury System (Ordinance No. 7500, 2020), art. 7**

- (1) For a grievance complaint on which the Committee has decided to apply the civil-complaints jury system, the Committee shall select a jury of not fewer than 5 and not more than 7 members, including one presiding juror.
- (2) The jury shall be selected from the candidate jury pool under art. 6, and shall include not fewer than 1 and not more than 3 members from each of the categories listed in art. 6(1).
- (3) When composing the jury, the Committee shall take into account the relevant field and expertise, and, for citizen jurors, shall take into account place of residence, age and gender.

**서울특별시 민원배심제 운영 조례 (서울특별시조례 제7500호, 2020), 제6조**

- ① 시장은 100명 이내의 범위에서 다음 각 호로 구성되는 배심원후보단을 구성할 수 있다.
    - 1\. 위원회 위원
    - 2\. 「서울특별시 시민감사옴부즈만위원회 운영 및 주민감사청구에 관한 조례」 제25조제1항에 따른 시민참여옴부즈만
    - 3\. 전문가배심원: 복지, 환경·교통, 주택·건축, 도시계획, 공공갈등 등 각 분야에서 교수, 변호사, 세무사, 기술사(건축사를 포함한다) 등의 자격과 실무경력을 두루 갖춘 전문가
    - 4\. 시민배심원: 「공직선거법」 제15조제2항에 따라 서울특별시의회 의원 및 시장의 선거권이 있는 사람
- ② 전문가배심원 및 시민배심원은 자치구 구청장 또는 관련 단체 등의 추천이나 공개모집 등의 방법과 위원회의 심의를 거쳐 시장이 위촉한다.
- ③ 전문가배심원 및 시민배심원의 임기는 2년으로 하되, 두 차례에 한하여 연임할 수 있다.

**서울특별시 민원배심제 운영 조례 (서울특별시조례 제7500호, 2020), 제7조**

- ① 위원회는 민원배심제를 실시하기로 결정한 고충민원에 대하여 대표배심원 1명을 포함한 5명 이상 7명 이내의 배심원단을 선정한다.
- ② 배심원단은 제6조에 따른 배심원후보단 중에서 선정하되, 제6조제1항 각 호에 따른 위원을 각각 1명 이상 3명 이내로 구성하여야 한다.
- ③ 위원회는 배심원단을 구성하는 경우 관련 분야 및 전문성을 고려하여야 하며, 시민배심원은 거주지, 연령, 성별 등을 고려하여야 한다.

The purpose of this ordinance is to set rules for operating the Civil-Complaints Jury so as to enhance citizen participation in the fair resolution of grievances.

**서울특별시 민원배심제 운영 조례 (서울특별시조례 제7500호, 2020), 제1조 (목적)**

The Itinerant Citizens' Assembly is a deliberative body that meets on several occasions during the term of the Council; it has thematic unity and coherence, and is composed of citizens chosen at random who rotate through the Assembly.

**Resolución 550 de 2020 del Concejo de Bogotá, art. 1, parágrafo**

La Asamblea Ciudadana Itinerante es un cuerpo deliberativo que se reúne en diversas ocasiones durante el periodo de la Corporación, tiene unidad temática y de sentido y se integra por ciudadanas y ciudadanos elegidos de manera aleatoria y que rotan por la Asamblea.

example: Deliberative Committees in the Walloon Parliament
nature_of_institutionalization: Permanently institutionalised since 2020 in the Rules of Procedure of the Walloon Parliament through Article 130 bis, which allows the creation of mixed deliberative committees of MPs and randomly selected citizens, triggered either by a simple majority of the Parliament's members or by a citizen petition of at least 2,000 signatories.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Rules of Procedure of the Walloon Parliament, Art. 130bis (introduced 2020), points 2, 8 and 17**

When it receives a citizen initiative, the Parliament decides within two months, on a report from the Conférence des présidents. (point 2)

Among the citizens drawn by lot who agree to take part in the deliberative committee, a second drawing of lots takes place to compose a group of 30 citizens, diverse and balanced at least in terms of gender, age, geographical distribution and level of education. (point 8)

Within six months of the tabling of the deliberative committee's report, the follow-up given to the recommendations is the subject of a reasoned report by the standing committee. … The standing committee's report is examined in plenary session. (point 17)

**Règlement du Parlement de Wallonie, article 130bis (inséré en 2020), points 2, 8 et 17**

Lorsqu'il est saisi d'une initiative citoyenne, le Parlement se prononce dans les deux mois, sur rapport de la Conférence des présidents. (point 2)

Parmi les citoyens tirés au sort marquant leur accord pour participer à la commission délibérative, un second tirage au sort a lieu afin de composer un groupe de 30 citoyens diversifiés et équilibrés au minimum en termes de genre, d'âge, de répartition géographique et de niveau de formation. (point 8)

Dans les six mois du dépôt du rapport de la commission délibérative, les suites qui ont été données aux recommandations font l'objet d'un rapport motivé de la commission permanente. … Le rapport de la commission permanente est examiné en séance plénière. (point 17)

legal_text_binding.text:
**Rules of Procedure of the Walloon Parliament, Art. 130bis (introduced 2020), points 1, 2 and 7**

The Parliament may, on the initiative of citizens or on the initiative of at least a simple majority of its members, establish a deliberative committee composed of deputies and citizens drawn by lot, to debate a specific issue of general interest and draw up proposed recommendations. (point 1)

To be admissible, the suggestion must: 1° be signed by at least 2,000 persons domiciled in the territory of the Walloon Region and aged 16 or over; … (point 2)

The deliberative committee is composed of: the deputies of the standing committee considered by the Conférence des présidents best placed to deal with the initiative; and 30 citizens designated by lot following the procedure in point 8. (point 7)

**Règlement du Parlement de Wallonie, article 130bis (inséré en 2020), points 1, 2 et 7**

Le Parlement peut, à l'initiative de citoyens ou à l'initiative d'au moins la majorité simple de ses membres, constituer une commission délibérative composée de députés et de citoyens tirés au sort pour débattre d'une problématique déterminée d'intérêt général et élaborer des propositions de recommandations. (point 1)

Pour être recevable, la suggestion doit : 1° être signée par au moins 2000 personnes domiciliées sur le territoire de la Région wallonne et âgées de 16 ans accomplis; … (point 2)

La commission délibérative est composée : des députés composant la commission permanente considérée par la Conférence des présidents comme la mieux à même de traiter l'initiative; et de 30 citoyens désignés par le sort suivant la procédure visée au point 8. (point 7)

nature_of_institutionalization: Decree of the Parliament creates a permanent 24-member Citizens' Council that mandates Citizens' Assemblies and ensures follow-up by Parliament and Government.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Decree introducing a permanent Citizens' Dialogue in the German-speaking Community (as amended 2024), Art. 6**

Parliament establishes the framework conditions for the organization of the Citizens' Dialogue. In its Rules of Procedure it organizes, in particular, the aspects of the Citizens' Dialogue that concern the parliamentary way of working. Parliament designates the bodies and persons that exercise the powers conferred on Parliament under the present Decree.

**Decree introducing a permanent Citizens' Dialogue in the German-speaking Community (as amended 2024), Art. 9**

After concluding its deliberations, the Citizens' Assembly formulates one or more recommendations, which are transmitted to Parliament. Parliament lays down in its Rules of Procedure the procedure for considering the recommendations and for taking them into account.

**Dekret zur Einführung eines permanenten Bürgerdialogs in der Deutschsprachigen Gemeinschaft (in der Fassung von 2024), Art. 6**

Das Parlament legt die Rahmenbedingungen für die Organisation des Bürgerdialogs fest. In seiner Geschäftsordnung organisiert es insbesondere die Aspekte des Bürgerdialogs, die die parlamentarische Arbeitsweise betreffen. Das Parlament bezeichnet die Gremien und Personen, die die Befugnisse wahrnehmen, die dem Parlament im vorliegenden Dekret zuerkannt werden.

**Dekret zur Einführung eines permanenten Bürgerdialogs in der Deutschsprachigen Gemeinschaft (in der Fassung von 2024), Art. 9**

Nach Abschluss der Beratungen formuliert die Bürgerversammlung eine oder mehrere Empfehlungen, die dem Parlament übermittelt werden. Das Parlament legt in seiner Geschäftsordnung das Verfahren zur Beratung der Empfehlungen und deren Berücksichtigung fest.

nature_of_institutionalization: Municipal regulation (Reglamento Orgánico) establishes a permanent, sortition-based body of some 49 residents to set the agenda for local referendums and make recommendations; members are drawn from the padrón (population register).

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 6(2)**

The persons who make up the City Observatory, as well as those who take part in its meetings and collaborate in its management, shall receive no remuneration for the exercise of their functions, except for the financial compensation due to them as attendance allowances for the body's meetings or any other indemnities. The Junta de Gobierno shall determine the amount of such compensation or indemnity.

**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 9**

1. The members (vocales) of the City Observatory shall be 49 full members and a minimum of 49 substitutes, men and women, constituting a demographically representative sample of the population of the City of Madrid.
2. The selection of the members shall be carried out as follows:
    - a significant number of households of persons registered in Madrid shall be selected, by a lottery that takes into account the geographical distribution of the population;
    - an invitation to participate as members shall be sent to these selected households;
    - the persons in these households who voluntarily accept the invitation shall enter a lottery that takes into account the demographic characteristics of the city of Madrid as regards age, sex and geographical distribution. In all cases, the same proportion of men and women as in the population of Madrid shall be guaranteed.
3. The appointment of the members and their substitutes shall be valid for one year, and once the office has been held it may not be held again. Persons holding a remunerated representative political office, holding public employment in the Madrid City Council, or more than one person per household, may not be members.

**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 14(1)**

The City Observatory shall convene the Plenary in ordinary session at least eight times a year. A constitutive session of the Plenary shall be held upon the appointment of the new members. In addition, an annual Plenary on municipal action shall be held before the end of the year of their appointment.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 6.2**

Las personas que integran el Observatorio de la Ciudad, así como quienes participen en sus reuniones y colaboren en su gestión, no percibirán retribución alguna por el ejercicio de sus funciones, salvo las compensaciones económicas que les correspondan como dietas de asistencia a las reuniones del órgano o cualesquiera otras indemnizaciones. Por Junta de Gobierno se determinará el importe de dicha compensación o indemnización.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 9**

1. Serán vocales del Observatorio de la Ciudad 49 personas titulares y un mínimo de 49 suplentes, hombres y mujeres, que supongan una muestra demográficamente representativa de la población de la Ciudad de Madrid.
2. La selección de las personas que serán vocales se realizará de la siguiente forma:
    - Se seleccionarán un número significativo de domicilios de personas empadronadas en Madrid, mediante un sorteo que tenga en cuenta la distribución geográfica de la población.
    - Se enviará una invitación para participar como vocales a estos domicilios seleccionados.
    - Las personas de estos domicilios que voluntariamente acepten esta invitación entrarán en un sorteo que tendrá en cuenta las características demográficas de la ciudad de Madrid referentes a la edad, sexo y distribución geográfica. En todo caso, se garantizará la misma proporción de hombres y mujeres que la existente en la población de Madrid.
3. El nombramiento de las vocalías y sus suplentes tendrá una vigencia de un año y una vez ejercido el cargo no podrán volver a ostentarlo de nuevo. No podrán ser vocales las personas que tengan cargo político representativo remunerado, tengan un empleo público en el Ayuntamiento de Madrid, o más de una persona por domicilio.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 14.1**

El Observatorio de la Ciudad reunirá el Plenario en sesión ordinaria al menos ocho veces al año. Se celebrará una sesión constitutiva del Plenario al producirse el nombramiento de los nuevos miembros. Además se celebrará un Plenario anual sobre la actuación municipal, antes de que finalice el año de su nombramiento.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 1**

This Regulation establishes and regulates the functioning of the City Observatory, as a citizen-participation body charged with analysing municipal action and its public policies.

**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 5(1)**

The City Observatory has as its purpose to monitor municipal action and its policies in order to make proposals for action. It also has as its purpose to channel citizen participation in the policies that affect their quality of life.

**Organic Regulation of the City Observatory (Madrid, 2019), art. 15(3)**

Within a maximum of 90 days after the issuance of the report of improvement recommendations, the Junta de Gobierno, or the body responsible depending on the subject matter of the recommendation, shall remit a formal response to all the recommendations and, where applicable, an action plan in that regard. Where the convening of public hearings has also been requested, the specific date of those consultations shall be specified.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 1**

El presente Reglamento establece y regula el funcionamiento del Observatorio de la Ciudad, como órgano de participación ciudadana encargado de analizar la acción municipal y sus políticas públicas.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 5.1**

El Observatorio de la Ciudad tiene como finalidad hacer un seguimiento de la acción municipal y de sus políticas al objeto de realizar propuestas de actuación. También tiene como finalidad encauzar la participación ciudadana en las políticas que afecten a su calidad de vida.

**Reglamento Orgánico del Observatorio de la Ciudad (Madrid, 2019), art. 15.3**

En el plazo máximo de 90 días posterior a la emisión del dictamen de recomendaciones de mejora, la Junta de Gobierno o el órgano que le corresponda, en función de la materia a la que se refiera la recomendación remitirá, una respuesta formal a todas las recomendaciones y, en su caso, un plan de actuación al respecto. En el caso de que también se hubiera requerido la convocatoria de audiencias públicas, se detallará la fecha concreta de dichas consultas.

example: Deliberative Committees in the Brussels Parliaments
nature_of_institutionalization: Permanently institutionalised by a 2019 ordinance of the Brussels Parliament (and copied into the rules of procedure of both the French Community Commission Parliament of Brussels and the Joint Community Commission Parliament), obliging Parliament to convene mixed citizen–MP deliberative committees.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Rules of Procedure of the Brussels-Capital Region Parliament (as amended 2019), Art. 25/1, points 2, 4–5 and 15**

Citizen suggestions are admissible if they are signed by at least 1,000 persons aged 16 or over residing in the Brussels-Capital Region, unless: … (point 2)

A deliberative committee is composed of the same deputies as the standing committee responsible for the subject being debated. … The deliberative committees invite 45 citizens to participate in their work. … a second drawing of lots takes place using a sampling method that fixes in advance the criteria ensuring a diverse and representative selection, at least in terms of gender, age, official languages of the Brussels-Capital Region, geographical distribution and level of education … (points 4–5)

The report is sent, for follow-up, to the standing committee having the same composition as the deliberative committee. … The report is presented by the standing committee in public session. … Within six months of the tabling of the report, the follow-up given to the recommendations is the subject of a follow-up report by the standing committee concerned. (point 15)

**Règlement du Parlement de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale (modification de 2019), article 25/1, points 2, 4–5 et 15**

Sont recevables, les suggestions citoyennes qui sont signées par au moins 1.000 personnes âgées de 16 ans accomplis et résidant dans la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale, sauf si : … (point 2)

Une commission délibérative est composée des mêmes députés que la commission permanente ayant dans ses attributions le sujet débattu. … Les commissions délibératives invitent 45 citoyens à participer à leurs travaux. … un second tirage au sort a lieu via une méthode d'échantillonnage fixant au préalable les critères assurant une sélection diverse et représentative, au moins en termes de genre, d'âge, de langues officielles de la Région de Bruxelles-Capitale, de répartition géographique et de niveau de formation … (points 4–5)

nature_of_institutionalization: Institutionalised at the provincial level through the Gipuzkoa Participation Regulation, embedding deliberative assemblies in governance.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Foral Law 5/2018 on Citizen Participation (Gipuzkoa), Article 13(3)–(6)**

Deliberative participation will require registration in the process by any citizen entities wishing to participate. This must guarantee the participation of entities that promote gender equality or have it as their mission.

The body responsible for citizen participation shall open a registration period of at least 30 calendar days for the entities referred to in Art. 8 (1 and 2) interested in taking part.

Individuals who can demonstrate a particular interest in the procedure may also participate. Before the process begins, the body responsible shall open a registration period for interested residents, determine the number of representatives, and appoint them according to the procedure defined in the protocol.

During the deliberative process, both the body responsible for citizen participation and participants can propose the addition of experts on the subject matter — including gender equality specialists — to ensure adequate technical support. Such decisions rest with the person responsible for managing the deliberative process and must be motivated.

**Norma Foral 5/2018, de 12 de noviembre, sobre Participación Ciudadana (Gipuzkoa), artículo 13, apartados 3–6**

La deliberación participativa exigirá, necesariamente, la inscripción en el proceso por parte de las entidades ciudadanas que así lo deseen. En este proceso, se garantizará la participación de entidades que desarrollen acciones para promover la igualdad de género o tengan la misma como misión.

El órgano competente en materia de participación ciudadana habilitará un período de inscripción, de 30 días naturales como mínimo, para las entidades señaladas en los apartados 1 y 2 del artículo 8 de esta norma foral que estén interesadas en intervenir en el proceso participativo.

En los procesos de deliberación participativa podrán también intervenir personas individuales que acrediten ostentar especial interés en el procedimiento. Antes de iniciarse un proceso participativo, el órgano competente en materia de participación ciudadana habilitará un período de inscripción de las personas residentes interesadas en el procedimiento, establecerá el número de personas que actuarán en representación de éstas y procederá a su designación de acuerdo con el procedimiento que determine en el protocolo.

Durante el desarrollo del proceso de deliberación participativa, tanto el órgano competente en materia de participación ciudadana como las personas que participan en el proceso podrán proponer la incorporación al mismo de personas expertas en la materia objeto de deliberación, incluyendo a especialistas en materia de igualdad de género, a los efectos de contar con el adecuado soporte técnico. La decisión sobre ello quedará en manos de la persona responsable del proceso de deliberación participativa, quien deberá motivar su decisión.

legal_text_binding.text:
**Foral Law 5/2018 on Citizen Participation (Gipuzkoa), Article 12**

Deliberative participatory processes are the set of acts integrated into a decision‑making procedure or determination of a specific public policy, whose content consists of public debate on the decision to be adopted and its characteristics, or on how to manage a certain action, as well as, where applicable, on the alternatives existing in this area, in which persons or citizen entities interested in the public or political decision to be adopted participate directly, in the forms and terms established in this Foral Norm.

The deliberative participatory processes regulated in this Foral Norm may be carried out within procedures related to the shaping of public policies that have special relevance or impact in the Historic Territory of Gipuzkoa and that fall under the competencies of the Foral Deputation as the executive body of government of that territory.

Deliberative participatory processes shall take place immediately after the start of the decision‑making or public policy formulation procedure and after the Foral Deputation of Gipuzkoa adopts the agreement that preliminarily sets out the basic characteristics of the public policy to be developed.

Exceptionally, deliberative participatory processes may also be carried out in successive phases of the procedure when the project or public policy to be adopted has acquired unforeseen significance during its processing or when its characteristics have been substantially transformed. In such cases, the initiative to carry out a deliberative participatory process must be expressly accepted by the Foral Commission for Citizen Participation. If the initiative is rejected by the Foral Commission, the rejection must be motivated.

**Norma Foral 5/2018, de 12 de noviembre, sobre Participación Ciudadana (Gipuzkoa), artículo 12**

Son procesos de deliberación participativa el conjunto de actos que se integran en un procedimiento de decisión o determinación de una concreta política pública, cuyo contenido consiste en un debate público sobre la decisión a adoptar y sus características o sobre la forma de gestionar una actuación determinada, así como, en su caso, sobre las alternativas existentes en este ámbito y en el que participan directamente personas o entidades ciudadanas interesadas en la decisión pública o política a adoptar, en las formas y términos establecidos en esta norma foral.

Los procesos de deliberación participativa que se regulan en esta norma foral podrán realizarse en el seno de procedimientos relativos a la determinación de las políticas públicas que tengan una especial relevancia o impacto en el Territorio Histórico de Gipuzkoa y que formen parte de las competencias que corresponden a la Diputación Foral en su condición de órgano ejecutivo de gobierno del mismo.

Los procesos de deliberación participativa se realizarán inmediatamente después del inicio del procedimiento de decisión o de formulación de una política pública y adopción por parte de la Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa del acuerdo que establezca, de forma preliminar, las características básicas de la política pública que se pretende desarrollar.

De forma excepcional, también podrán realizarse procesos de deliberación participativa en fases sucesivas del procedimiento cuando el proyecto o política pública a adoptar haya adquirido durante su tramitación una trascendencia imprevista en el momento inicial o cuando las características del mismo se hayan transformado de forma sustancial. En estos supuestos, la iniciativa para realizar un proceso de deliberación participativa deberá ser expresamente aceptada por la Comisión Foral para la Participación Ciudadana. La desestimación de la iniciativa por parte de la Comisión Foral deberá estar motivada.

**Guideline of the Vorarlberg State Government on the Convening and Conduct of Citizens' Councils 2013, § 5a(6)–(7)**

6. A Citizens' Council that addresses matters of state legislation or state administration must be convened if this is
    1. requested in writing by at least 1,000 eligible citizens, including their names and addresses,
    2. decided by the State Parliament (Landtag), or
    3. decided by the State Government.
7. A Citizens' Council dealing with an issue of municipal administration must be convened if the affected municipality (or municipalities) requests it by a resolution of the municipal council.

**Guideline of the Vorarlberg State Government on the Convening and Conduct of Citizens' Councils 2013, § 5b**

1. The organization of the Citizens' Council process is the responsibility of the Office for Future-related Issues (Büro für Zukunftsfragen).
2. Once the prerequisites under § 5a(6) and (7) are met, the Office must select eligible participants (per § 5a(5)) from the affected region and invite them to the Citizens' Council.

4) The selection of eligible participants is based on the population register or electoral roll for the respective region.
5) In the random selection, maximum diversity must be ensured. Therefore, the criteria of age and gender must be taken into account in the selection.
6) For process quality, the Office for Future-related Issues must provide a suitable venue and ensure that the Citizens' Council is moderated by one or more independent persons, in adherence to the principle of objectivity, using the Dynamic Facilitation method. The involvement of experts and information providers is permissible.
7) The Office for Future-related Issues must summarize the outcome of the Citizens' Council in a report. This report must, at minimum, include:
    1. the name(s) of the moderator(s);
    2. the names of the Citizens' Council participants;
    3. the essential course of the process;
    4. any suggestions — such suggestions require the approval of all participants;
    5. the signatures of the moderator(s) and the participants.

**Richtlinie der Vorarlberger Landesregierung zur Einberufung und Durchführung von Bürgerräten 2013, § 5a Abs. 6–7**

6. Ein Bürgerrat, der Angelegenheiten der Landesgesetzgebung oder der Landesverwaltung berührt, ist abzuhalten, wenn dies
    1. von wenigstens 1000 teilnahmeberechtigten Bürgerinnen und Bürgern unterschriftlich unter Angabe des Namens und der Anschrift verlangt wird,
    2. vom Landtag beschlossen wird oder
    3. von der Landesregierung beschlossen wird.
7. Ein Bürgerrat in einer Angelegenheit der Gemeindeverwaltung ist abzuhalten, wenn dies von der betroffenen Gemeinde oder den betroffenen Gemeinden aufgrund eines Gemeindevertretungsbeschlusses verlangt wird.

**Richtlinie der Vorarlberger Landesregierung zur Einberufung und Durchführung von Bürgerräten 2013, § 5b**

1. Die Organisation des Bürgerratsprozesses obliegt dem Büro für Zukunftsfragen.
2. Das Büro für Zukunftsfragen hat bei Vorliegen der Voraussetzungen nach § 5a Abs. 6 und Abs. 7 teilnahmeberechtigte Personen (§ 5a Abs. 5) des betroffenen Gebietes auszuwählen und zum Bürgerrat einzuladen.

4) Die Auswahl der teilnahmeberechtigten Personen erfolgt auf Basis des Melderegisters/Wählerverzeichnisses für das betroffene Gebiet.
5) Bei der Zufallsauswahl ist auf eine größtmögliche Diversität zu achten. Daher ist es notwendig, die Kriterien Alter und Geschlecht bei der Auswahl zu berücksichtigen.
6) Im Sinne der Prozessqualität hat das Büro für Zukunftsfragen für einen geeigneten Veranstaltungsort zu sorgen, sowie dass der Bürgerrat durch eine oder mehrere unabhängige Personen unter Beachtung des Grundsatzes der Objektivität und mit der Moderationsmethode Dynamic Facilitation moderiert wird. Die Beiziehung von Sachverständigen und Auskunftspersonen ist zulässig.
7) Das Ergebnis des Bürgerrates ist durch das Büro für Zukunftsfragen in einem Bericht zusammenzufassen. Dieser Bericht hat jedenfalls zu enthalten
    1. den Namen der Person oder der Personen, die den Bürgerrat moderieren;
    2. die Namen der Bürgerräte;
    3. den wesentlichen Verlauf des Prozesses;
    4. allfällige Anregungen; solche Anregungen bedürfen der Zustimmung aller Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer;
    5. die Unterschrift der Moderatorinnen und Moderatoren (lit. a) und der Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer (lit. b).

nature_of_institutionalization: Oregon's Citizens' Initiative Review is a legally mandated process where randomly selected panels of 18-24 representative citizens deliberate for 3-5 days on ballot measures and produce statements for the voters' pamphlet to help inform fellow voters.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**ORS 250.139(4)(a)**

The commission shall select citizens for each panel from a representative sample of anonymous electors, using survey sampling methods that, to the extent practicable, give every elector a similar chance of being selected. Each citizen panel shall consist of not fewer than 18 and not more than 24 electors.

**ORS 250.139(6)(a)**

Each panel shall meet to review the measure on not fewer than three and not more than five consecutive days for a total of not less than 24 hours unless otherwise provided by commission rule.

legal_text_binding.text:
**ORS 250.137(1)**

The Citizens' Initiative Review Commission is established as a semi-independent state agency subject to ORS 182.456 to 182.472. The commission shall consist of 11 members.

**ORS 250.141(4)**

The secretary shall provide with any citizen panel statement a description of not more than 150 words of the citizen panel process described in ORS 250.137 to 250.149 and the following explanation:

…

The opinions expressed in this statement are those of the members of a citizen panel and were developed through the citizen review process. They are NOT official opinions or positions endorsed by the State of Oregon or any government agency. A citizen panel is not a judge of the constitutionality or legality of any ballot measure, and any statements about such matters are not binding on a court of law.

nature_of_institutionalization: Institutionalised by municipal ordinance providing for citizen deliberation meetings on key policies.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Yoshikawa City Citizen Participation Ordinance 2004 (as amended 2011), Art. 29**

1. When a city organ selects participants for a citizen deliberation meeting, it shall invite applicants from among citizens chosen at random from the Basic Resident Register, and appoint them.
2. Where the number of applicants exceeds the quota for the citizen deliberation meeting to be held, the city organ may select participants by lot.
3. The city organ shall pay an honorarium to the participants.

**Yoshikawa City Citizen Participation Ordinance 2004 (as amended 2011), Art. 30**

1. The city organ shall make the citizen deliberation meeting public and, when holding it, shall publish in advance the date and time, venue, content and other matters, as prescribed by rule.
2. When the city organ has held a citizen deliberation meeting, it shall prepare and publish a record of the meeting, as prescribed by rule; however, non-public information shall not be published.

**吉川市市民参画条例（平成16年制定・平成23年改正）第29条**

1. 市の機関は、市民討議会の参加者を選任する場合は、住民基本台帳により無作為で選ばれた市民の中から参加希望者を募り、選任するものとします。
2. 市の機関は、参加希望者が、実施しようとする市民討議会の定員を超えた場合は、抽選により参加者を選任することができるものとします。
3. 市の機関は、参加者に謝礼を支払うものとします。

**吉川市市民参画条例（平成16年制定・平成23年改正）第30条**

1. 市の機関は、市民討議会を公開し、市民討議会を開催するときは、規則で定めるところにより開催日時、開催場所、内容などを事前に公表するものとします。
2. 市の機関は、市民討議会を開催したときは、規則で定めるところにより開催記録を作成し、公表するものとします。ただし、非公開情報は、公表しないものとします。

When a city organ seeks to hear unbiased opinions, proposals and the like from citizens on a matter, it shall hold a citizen deliberation meeting (shimin tōgikai).

**吉川市市民参画条例（平成16年制定・平成23年改正）第28条**

市の機関は、事案に対し、偏りのない意見、提案などを市民から聴取しようとする場合は、市民討議会を開催します。

nature_of_institutionalization: Permanence is constitutionally mandated in Georgia, where grand juries are empaneled regularly in every county and given statutory duties beyond indictments, including ongoing oversight of local government institutions.

legal_text_process_design.text:
**Ga. Code § 15-12-71(b)(1)**

The grand jury shall at least once in each calendar year inspect the condition and operations of the county jail. The grand jury shall at least once in every three calendar years inspect and examine the offices and operations of the clerk of superior court, the judge of the probate court, and the county treasurer or county depository. If the office of the district attorney is located in the county in which the grand jury is impaneled, the grand jury shall inspect and examine the offices of the district attorney at least once in every three calendar years. If the offices of the district attorney are located in a county other than the county in which the grand jury is impaneled, the grand jury may inspect the offices of the district attorney as the grand jury deems necessary or desirable.

**Ga. Code § 15-12-71(b)(2)**

In addition to the inspections provided for in paragraph (1) of this subsection, the grand jury shall, whenever deemed necessary by eight or more of its members, appoint a committee of its members to inspect or investigate any county office or county public building or any public authority of the county or the office of any county officer, any court or court official of the county, the county board of education, or the county school superintendent or any of the records, accounts, property, or operations of any of the foregoing.

**Ga. Code § 15-12-71(b)(3)**

The grand jury may prepare reports or issue presentments … subject to publication …

legal_text_binding.text:
**Georgia Constitution, Art. I, Sec. I, Para. XI(c)**

The General Assembly shall provide by law for the selection and compensation of persons to serve as grand jurors and trial jurors.

*Note: the Georgia Constitution just sets out that the General Assembly should provide for the selection of grand jurors. Their actual role is defined in the separate code — see previous column.*
